text: It seems clear to me that in politics, consistent rules beat flashy reforms. A lot of the conversation focuses on surface drama, but the deeper mechanics rarely get attention. When incentives are misaligned, people respond in predictable ways, and then everyone acts surprised. I get why some people argue that short term wins can build momentum. There are moments when disruption shakes loose outdated habits, and that energy can be useful. Still, without guardrails and follow through, momentum fades fast. In my view, acknowledging both sides actually makes the argument stronger instead of weaker. At the end of the day, steady progress beats chaos.

There are moments when disruption shakes loose outdated habits, and that energy can be useful. Still, without guardrails and follow through, momentum fades fast. In my view, acknowledging both sides actually makes the argument stronger instead of weaker. At the end of the day, steady progress beats chaos.
